title: Segmented key-value cache low-precision profiles and perf/quality surface
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Experimental sweep to generate a performance/quality surface for low-precision profiles applied to the model key-value cache. We will evaluate segmented profiles (by token position ranges), per-layer sensitivity, and per-head fallbacks. Deliverables: calibrated profile set, validation reports, runtime selection heuristic, and rollout playbook.
objectives: Build a matrix of FP8 vs INT8 profiles across position segments (e.g., prefix 0..64, 65..256, >256) and model layers to measure latency, p95/p99, throughput, and quality delta.
Validate a calibration workflow that produces per-profile scale factors and bias compensation suitable for shadow validation and can be applied at runtime with low overhead.
Produce decision rules for runtime profile selection (static mapping, sequence-length gating, or soft gating with confidence threshold).
Quantify cost impact and SLO risks; define rollback and mitigation strategies for customer-facing deployments.
hypothesis: Segmented position-based FP8 profiles combined with INT8 on early layers will yield majority of token-latency improvements while keeping end-user quality regressions under 1% absolute for most generation tasks.
Per-head sensitivity is concentrated in a small subset of attention heads; selectively keeping these heads at higher precision prevents the largest quality regressions with minimal latency cost.
datasets_and_eval_sets: Internal LLM-eval harness: summarization, instruction following, code generation, and dialogue (10k prompts total).
Customer-like production shard: anonymized prefix distribution (2M tokens) sampled from hosted API telemetry for representative sequence lengths.
Holdout regression suite: 1k reference prompts used for A/B perplexity, ROUGE-L, exact-match, and instruction-compliance heuristics.
calibration_workflow: Offline activation capture: run representative batches in FP32 to collect per-layer activation histograms and per-head value ranges.
Profile generator: compute scale/zero-point and FP8 exponent bias compensation for each candidate profile (segment x layer x head mask).
Shadow validation: deploy profiles in shadow runner (no customer impact) comparing logits drift, token-level KL, and downstream metric deltas.
Automated rejection criteria: reject any profile with >2% relative increase in perplexity or >1.5% drop in exact-match on holdout.
metrics: Latency: median token latency, p95, p99 (ms)
Throughput: tokens/sec and GPU utilization under steady-state batching
Quality: delta perplexity (PPL), delta ROUGE-L, delta exact-match, token-level KL and top-1 logit shift
Operational: cost per 1M tokens, memory delta for KV cache, failure/rollback rate in shadow runs
success_criteria: Find at least one segmented profile that reduces median token latency by >=12% vs baseline FP32/INT16 KV while keeping holdout quality regressions within defined thresholds (per-metric thresholds in calibration_workflow).
Runtime selection heuristic can be implemented with <1% extra CPU overhead and no impact to existing p95 latency SLOs in Dedicated tier tests.
Clear rollback and canary test steps documented for Console rollout.
experiment_plan: Phase 1 (2025-02-12 .. 2025-02-20): activation capture across representative models (gather histograms, per-head stats).
Phase 2 (2025-02-21 .. 2025-02-28): offline profile generation and small-scale shadow runs (10k prompts).
Phase 3 (2025-03-01 .. 2025-03-07): large-scale sweep across segments and hybrid head masks, measure latency/quality surface.
Phase 4 (2025-03-08 .. 2025-03-14): select candidate profiles, implement runtime selection heuristic, and run canary in Dedicated environment.
early_findings_and_notes: 2025-02-25 - Diego Martinez: initial small-scale shadow run shows FP8 across late-position segments (>=256) provides ~18% median token latency reduction but incurs a 0.9% drop in exact-match on code generation tasks.

2025-02-27 - Aisha Raman: per-head analysis identified ~6 heads in middle layers with outsized sensitivity; masking those heads to INT8 while applying FP8 elsewhere reduces exact-match delta to 0.3% while preserving 14% latency win.
2025-03-03 - Performance team: NVidia kernel scheduling variance visible at sequence lengths >1024; need to factor micro-batching policies into throughput measurement to avoid noisy p99 results.
2025-03-04 - Product (L. Chen): flagging customer impact for instruction-following workloads — propose stricter acceptance thresholds for conversational models used in Hosted tier.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quality regressions on edge-case prompts (long-tail) not seen in holdout; Mitigation: extended shadow run with adversarial prompt set and automatic rollback triggers.
Risk: Runtime overhead for dynamic gating increasing CPU latency; Mitigation: implement a simple static mapping fallback and measure CPU p95 before attempting soft gating.
Risk: Drift over time as token distributions shift; Mitigation: schedule nightly recalibration on a rolling window and add a drift monitor dashboard.
runtime_plan_and_rollout: Create a profile registry in control plane with profile metadata (segment ranges, layer masks, calibration stats, approved flag).
Implement runtime heuristic: sequence-length -> profile mapping with optional per-request confidence check producing "rollback_flag" when drift metric exceeds threshold.
Canary steps: Dedicated 10% traffic -> monitor quality/regression metrics for 48h -> expand to 50% if stable -> Hosted limited beta by invite.
